deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no derivation by Ramanujan. It is a short referee's or reader's note, in a hand other than Ramanujan's, commenting on a submitted paper, probably the one whose problem appears on the next folio. The pencil shelfmark 'Add. Ms a 94^{18(12)}' is written top right. The note reads: 'Paper a little difficult to understand after the 1st page. I don't see where eqn (12) comes from, & m = 5, k = 8 (quoted on page 3) does not come from the value of k given [x/m], as x is -ve.'

The mathematical point is as follows. The paper apparently defines an integer k = [x/m], with [ ] the integer-part (floor) function. If x < 0 and m = 5 > 0, then x/m < 0, so [x/m] <= -1. A positive value such as k = 8 therefore cannot arise from that formula. The referee is flagging that the worked example on p.3 is inconsistent with the paper's own definition. Two further complaints are made: equation (12) is unjustified, and the exposition is obscure after page 1. The previous fragment ('Is there not a confusion ... on p 3, near bottom') belongs to the same report.

Context (the next page, not this one): the paper maximises e(1-e)(1-2e) over e = n/m with integer n. The unconstrained maximum is at e = (3-sqrt3)/6, with value 1/(6 sqrt3). The paper gives the closed form n = [(m+1)/2 - sqrt((m^2-1)/12)]. It tabulates v_m = n(m-n)(m-2n)/m^3 as 0, 0, 2/27, 6/64, 12/125, 20/216, 30/343, 48/512, 70/729, 96/1000 for m = 1 to 10. I spot-checked these by hand and they are correct. The 'x', 'k' and 'eqn (12)' of the referee's note presumably refer to a later part of that paper not transcribed here.
errors: No mathematical content of the author's on this page to check. The referee's objection itself is valid: if x < 0 and m > 0, then floor(x/m) is negative, so k = 8 with m = 5 cannot come from k = [x/m] unless the paper intends a different convention (e.g. |x|, or a sign error in the paper).

results.what: Referee's remark that k = [x/m] is negative for negative x, so the quoted example m=5, k=8 is inconsistent
results.modern_name: Property of the floor function (sign of floor of a negative number)
